key_insight: A deep neural operator can learn to solve free-boundary PDEs—predicting both field values and moving boundaries—with high precision, enabling real-time simulation such as tumour-growth forecasting.
problem_solved: Free-boundary problems (PDEs with moving interfaces) are hard to solve accurately and quickly using classical numerical methods because of mesh re‑generation, coupling between field and boundary evolution, and high computational cost—limiting real-time and clinical use.
method: Train a deep neural operator to map inputs (initial conditions, parameters, boundary/geometry cues) to solution fields and the evolving free boundary.
Use a geometry-aware/implicit boundary representation and a combined data- and physics-driven loss to enforce PDE and interface consistency.
Validate and calibrate the operator with simulation/clinical-relevant datasets to achieve high accuracy and fast inference for downstream prediction tasks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable, generalizable approach to model complex moving-boundary physics for real-time applications (e.g., digital twins and clinical decision support), lowering compute cost and enabling rapid parameter studies and uncertainty quantification.
visual_elements: Schematic: neural operator block mapping inputs (params, initial state) to evolving field + moving boundary
Sequence frames: time-lapse simulation of tumour growth comparing ground-truth PDE solver vs neural operator
Performance chart: accuracy vs runtime (neural operator vs traditional solvers)

paper_title: Deep neural operator for free boundary problems
paper_authors: Zongjia Long, Qi Zhou, Aiqing Zhu, Dong Dai, Yiqun Liu
